item.text:
**New Accepted Sources**
- `S027` (`C047`): *Russian Federation: New Law Introduces Electronic Summons for Conscripts* | Library of Congress | 2023-07-11 | https://www.loc.gov/item/global-legal-monitor/2023-07-10/russian-federation-new-law-introduces-electronic-summons-for-conscripts/ | source type: secondary legal monitor | confidence: high, because it is a US government legal summary of a Putin-signed law | final evidence use: mobilization, draft enforcement, administrative coercion | language: English | locator: `turn24view3` L39-L41, L52-L57 and `turn24view4` L39-L41 | supported claims: Putin signed Federal Law No. 127-FZ on 14 April 2023; it created electronic summons, a unified registry, and penalties/constraints for evaders | temporal fit: direct 2023 | Putin attribution: direct signature | limitations: not the statute text itself, but a reliable legal monitor summary | contrary considerations: none in the item | 2B lenses: L2, L5, L8, L9, L10
- `S028` (`C049`): *THE SECRETARY-GENERAL -- REMARKS TO THE PRESS* | United Nations in Ukraine | 2023-03-08 | https://ukraine.un.org/en/222286-secretary-general-remarks-press | source type: primary UN press release | confidence: high | final evidence use: diplomacy, ceasefire framing, accountability, ZNPP safety, grain corridor, prisoner exchanges | language: English | locator: `turn28view0` L69-L115 | supported claims: Russia’s invasion violates the UN Charter and international law; just peace must be based on the Charter; UN was working on humanitarian aid, Azovstal evacuations, Black Sea grain exports, ZNPP demilitarization, POW exchanges, and accountability | temporal fit: direct 2023 | Putin attribution: indirect, through Russia state action | limitations: UN institutional perspective | contrary considerations: acknowledges humanitarian relief and negotiation channels | 2B lenses: L1, L4, L5, L6, L7, L9, L10
- `S029` (`C050`): *Moscow Mechanism: "Report on Violations and Abuses of International Humanitarian and Human Rights Law, War Crimes and Crimes Against Humanity, related to the Forcible Transfer and/or Deportation of Ukrainian Children to the Russian Federation"* | OSCE ODIHR | 2023-05-04 | https://odihr.osce.org/odihr/542751 | source type: expert mission report landing page | confidence: medium-high, because I verified the OSCE mission page and topic, but only landing-page metadata in this turn | final evidence use: child transfer/deportation, occupation coercion, IHL framing | language: English | locator: `turn20view7` L61-L69 | supported claims: OSCE expert mission report exists on forcible transfer/deportation of Ukrainian children to the Russian Federation | temporal fit: direct 2023 | Putin attribution: indirect via Russian state/occupation policy | limitations: landing-page metadata only, not the full report text | contrary considerations: the title reflects allegations, not a criminal conviction | 2B lenses: L2, L4, L5, L9, L10
- `S030` (`C051`): *OSCE human rights office monitoring finds evidence of torture and sexual violence in Ukraine as violations continue* | OSCE ODIHR | 2023-07-17 | https://odihr.osce.org/odihr/548662 | source type: press release / monitoring summary | confidence: high | final evidence use: civilian harm, detention abuse, accountability | language: English | locator: `turn20view6` L75-L84 | supported claims: arbitrary imprisonment, enforced disappearances, torture, sexual violence, summary executions, forcible displacement, and intensified attacks on civilians and civilian objects by Russian forces | temporal fit: direct 2023 | Putin attribution: indirect, via Russian armed forces and occupation structures | limitations: monitoring summary, not a criminal judgment | contrary considerations: notes reports of ill-treatment of Russian POWs by Ukraine too | 2B lenses: L2, L4, L5, L9, L10
- `S031` (`C052`): *Update on the human rights situation in Ukraine, 1 February 2023 – 30 April 2023* | OHCHR / HRMMU | 2023-06-13 | https://ukraine.ohchr.org/en/update-human-rights-situation-ukraine-1-february-2023-30-april-2023-EN | source type: UN human rights report | confidence: high | final evidence use: passportization, coercion in occupied areas, deportation risk, religious repression | language: English | locator: `turn20view0` L83-L84 and `turn20view1` L84-L85 | supported claims: a Putin decree pressured occupied residents toward Russian passports and exposed some to deportation/forcible transfer risk; violence against UOC members/supporters increased | temporal fit: direct 2023 | Putin attribution: direct to the President’s decree and the occupation framework | limitations: mid-2023 reporting window | contrary considerations: explicitly notes the decree does not itself impose citizenship | 2B lenses: L2, L4, L5, L6, L7, L9, L10
- `S032` (`C053`): *Protection of Civilians in Armed Conflict — December 2023* | OHCHR / HRMMU | 2024-01-15 | https://ukraine.ohchr.org/en/protection-civilians-armed-conflict-december-2023-EN | source type: UN human rights report | confidence: high | final evidence use: year-end civilian casualty trend and Russian strike pattern | language: English | locator: `turn20view2` L82-L85 | supported claims: at least 592 civilians were killed or injured in December 2023; the increase was driven mainly by intensified Russian missile and loitering-munition attacks on 29 and 30 December | temporal fit: directly reports December 2023 facts | Putin attribution: indirect through Russian armed forces | limitations: published in January 2024, but the factual window is December 2023 | contrary considerations: most casualties occurred in government-controlled territory too | 2B lenses: L2, L4, L5, L9, L10
- `S033` (`C054`): *Russia - Ukraine international armed conflict: ICRC continues to help people in need* | ICRC | 2023-06-14 | https://www.icrc.org/en/document/russia-ukraine-international-armed-conflict-icrc-continues-to-help-people-in-need | source type: humanitarian operational report | confidence: high | final evidence use: civilian protection, humanitarian access, POWs, water, mine risk | language: English | locator: `turn20view4` L218-L236 and `turn20view5` L235-L236 | supported claims: ICRC visited over 1,500 POWs, helped 5,500 families, brought safe drinking water to over 1.9 million people since the start of 2023, and delivered cash aid, food, and hygiene support | temporal fit: direct 2023 | Putin attribution: indirect, as a consequence of the war and occupation conditions | limitations: humanitarian actor, not an attribution or law-enforcement body | contrary considerations: emphasizes aid and contact across frontlines rather than blame | 2B lenses: L1, L4, L5, L7, L9, L10
- `S034` (`C055`): *Human rights situation during the Russian occupation of territory of Ukraine and its aftermath, 24 February 2022 to 31 December 2023* | OHCHR / HRMMU | 2024-03-20 | https://ukraine.ohchr.org/en/human-rights-situation-during-russian-occupation-territory-ukraine-and-its-aftermath-EN | source type: thematic UN human rights report | confidence: high | final evidence use: occupation administration, coercion, Russification, accountability | language: English | locator: `turn27view0` L83-L102 | supported claims: systematic dismantling of rights in occupied territory, coercive governance changes, Russian legal framework imposition, passport-based discrimination, forced Russian curriculum, child enlistment, and the need for Russian withdrawal and accountability | temporal fit: covers through 31 Dec 2023 | Putin attribution: indirect but strongly state-policy linked | limitations: published in 2024 and retrospective over occupied territory; Russia did not provide access to occupied areas | contrary considerations: notes possible overbreadth in some Ukrainian collaboration prosecutions | 2B lenses: L2, L4, L5, L6, L7, L9, L10
- `S035` (`C056`): *Russia's Putin: Black Sea grain deal became meaningless* | Reuters wire, mirrored by Investing.com | 2023-07-23 | https://www.investing.com/news/commodities-news/russias-putin-black-sea-grain-deal-became-meaningless-3131719 | source type: wire-service mirror | confidence: medium-high, because the article is Reuters content and I opened the mirrored publication | final evidence use: Putin’s public justification for quitting the grain deal and the coercive food-security framing | language: English | locator: `turn24view0` L418-L432 and `turn24view1` L418-L423 | supported claims: Putin said the deal lost its humanitarian meaning, Russia quit after its conditions were ignored, Russia would keep supplying grain to Africa, and Russian strikes on Ukrainian food-export ports continued | temporal fit: direct 2023 | Putin attribution: direct quote via Reuters | limitations: mirror URL rather than the original Reuters URL | contrary considerations: article itself notes the humanitarian purpose of the deal and the post-withdrawal strikes on Ukrainian ports | 2B lenses: L1, L2, L4, L6, L7, L10
